mainTopic: Spending on שבת and יום טוב, the gift of שבת and the נשמה יתירה, and which foods are valid for עירובי תבשילין.
overview: This amud opens with a teaching that a person's yearly income is set between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים, except what he spends on שבת, יום טוב, and his sons' תלמוד תורה. For those, Heaven matches his income to his spending. רבי אבהו brings the source from תהלים, and the גמרא proves that חֹק means a food portion. A ברייתא then contrasts שמאי הזקן, who saved his best food for שבת all week, with הלל הזקן, who trusted ה׳ day by day. Next, רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says a giver need not tell the receiver about a gift. The גמרא challenges this from ה׳ announcing the gift of שבת and settles it: a gift that will become known needs no announcement, but a hidden one does, and the reward of שבת is hidden. רבי שמעון בן יוחי teaches that שבת was given privately, and ריש לקיש describes the נשמה יתירה given on שבת. The גמרא then returns to עירובי תבשילין: אביי rules that bread is not valid, and two versions give different reasons. The amud ends with leftover foods that can serve as the עירוב and with small salted fish cooked by a גוי, and the last discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Yearly income is fixed, except spending for שבת, יום טוב, and תלמוד תורה
steps.stepSummary: A person's yearly income is set from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים, except money spent on שבת, יום טוב, and his sons' תלמוד תורה. For these, more spending brings more income, and less spending brings less.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of a person's food and income is fixed for him from ראש השנה until יום הכפורים, except what he spends for שבתות, what he spends for יום טוב, and what he spends on his sons' תלמוד תורה. If he spends less on these, they give him less; if he spends more, they give him more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a teaching about how a person's income is decided each year, with three special exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally your yearly earnings are decided during the ימי הדין. But spending on שבת, יום טוב, and Torah learning is not fixed ahead of time. Heaven matches your income to what you actually spend on them, so spending more on these never leaves you short.

keyTerms.meaning: תלמוד תורה (here, paying for one's sons' learning)

steps.confusionAlert: 'They reduce for him' does not mean he is punished. It means Heaven simply gives him less extra money because he spent less on these מצוות. The extra income exists only to cover the extra spending.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching encourages spending generously on כבוד שבת ויום טוב and on Torah education, even borrowing for them, with trust that the money will be covered.

phrases.english: All of a person's food (livelihood)
is fixed for him
from Rosh HaShanah until Yom Kippur,
except for expenses for Shabbatot
and expenses for Yom Tov
and expenses for his sons' Torah study,
for if he spent less, they give him less,
phrases.notes: Heaven lowers his income to match.

phrases.english: and if he spent more, they give him more.
phrases.notes: Heaven raises his income to cover it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם קְצוּבִים לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage. It continues the earlier theme of honoring שבת and יום טוב with food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Income is fixed yearly, except spending on שבת, יום טוב, and children's תלמוד תורה, which Heaven matches to actual spending.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's verse: ראש השנה is a חֹק for ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings the פסוק source. 'בַּכֵּסֶא' (the covered moon) points to ראש השנה, and the next פסוק calls it a חֹק, which hints at food being decided then.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: What is the verse for this? 'Blow the שופר on the new month, at the covered time, for our festival day.' Which festival has the moon covered? You must say it is ראש השנה. And it is written next: 'For it is a חֹק for ישראל, a judgment of the God of יעקב.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו asks for the פסוק behind the teaching and answers with two פסוקים from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only חג that falls on the first of the month, when the moon is still hidden, is ראש השנה. The very next פסוק says that day is a חֹק and a משפט, meaning a day of judgment about one's חֹק. The next step explains why חֹק means food.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say (only one option fits)
A statute; also an allotted portion

steps.confusionAlert: The word in parentheses, (בַּכֵּסֶא), is the פסוק's own word, written as 'בַּכֶּסֶה'. The דרשה reads it as 'covered', not 'chair'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
What is the verse (for this)?
"Blow the shofar on the new month,
phrases.notes: תהלים פא:ד

phrases.english: at the covered time, for our festival day,"
Which festival is the one on which the moon is covered?
You must say: this is Rosh HaShanah,
phrases.notes: Other festivals fall mid-month, when the moon is visible.

phrases.english: and it is written: "For it is a chok for Israel,
phrases.notes: תהלים פא:ה

phrases.english: a judgment of the God of Jacob."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the teaching in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That a person's livelihood (חֹק) is judged on ראש השנה.

steps.title: How do we know חֹק means food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the word חֹק in רבי אבהו's פסוק refers to food.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we see that this word חֹק is a term for food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to check one step of רבי אבהו's proof. This line sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's proof only works if חֹק means a food portion and not just 'law'. The גמרא asks for evidence of that meaning.

phrases.english: From where is it implied
that this word 'chok' is a term for food?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי חֹק לִישָּׁנָא דִּמְזוֹנֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions a key word in the proof of step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A proof that חֹק means food.

steps.title: Proof from פרעה's food allotment
steps.stepSummary: In בראשית, the Egyptian priests 'ate their חֹק that פרעה gave them'. So חֹק means a food portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they ate their allotment (חֻקָּם) that פרעה gave them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק from בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק directly links eating with חֻקָּם, so חֹק means an allotted portion of food. This confirms רבי אבהו's reading.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And they ate their allotment
phrases.notes: בראשית מז:כב

phrases.english: that Pharaoh gave them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חֹק means a food portion, as in בראשית מז:כב.

steps.title: מר זוטרא's proof: 'my allotted bread'
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא brings a different proof from משלי: 'Feed me my חֹק bread'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: From here: 'Feed me my allotted (חֻקִּי) bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא offers a second, alternative answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here חֻקִּי is attached directly to לֶחֶם (bread), which may be an even clearer link to food. The conclusion is the same: חֹק means a food portion.
steps.whatToRemember: ראש השנה is called a חֹק, meaning a food portion, so on that day a person's livelihood is decided.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: from here:
"Feed me my allotted bread."
phrases.notes: משלי ל:ח

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same answer as step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חֹק means food, as in משלי ל:ח.

steps.title: שמאי הזקן saved his best food for שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says שמאי הזקן ate all week in honor of שבת. He set aside a nice animal for שבת, and if he found a nicer one, he saved that one and ate the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: They said about שמאי הזקן that all his days he ate in honor of שבת. If he found a nice animal, he said: 'This is for שבת.' If he found another one nicer than it, he set aside the second and ate the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא describing שמאי הזקן's practice of honoring שבת all week long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי always kept the best animal for שבת. Whenever he upgraded, he ate the earlier one during the week. So even his weekday meals were part of preparing for כבוד שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: 'Set aside the second' means he saved the second, nicer animal for שבת. It does not mean he gave it up.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן,
phrases.english: It was taught: They said about Shammai the Elder

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יָמָיו הָיָה אוֹכֵל לִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: that all his days he ate in honor of Shabbat.
If he found a nice animal,
he would say: "This is for Shabbat."
If he found another one nicer than it,
he set aside the second (for Shabbat)
and ate the first.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from spending on שבת to a model of honoring שבת every day of the week.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמאי הזקן always saved the best food for שבת, so all his eating was לכבוד שבת.

steps.title: הלל's different approach: trusting ה׳ every day
steps.stepSummary: Unlike שמאי, הלל הזקן did not save the best food for שבת all week. All his actions were לשם שמים, and he trusted ה׳ day by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But הלל הזקן had a different way. All his actions were for the sake of Heaven, as the פסוק says: 'Blessed is ה׳ day by day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from שמאי's practice (step 6) and contrasts it with הלל's practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי planned all week for שבת. הלל did not stockpile. He trusted that ה׳ would provide something good for שבת when the time came, so each day could be handled on its own. The פסוק 'ברוך ה׳ יום יום' means ה׳ gives a blessing every single day.
steps.confusionAlert: הלל is not less careful about honoring שבת. He has a different kind of trust (בטחון) that ה׳ will provide for שבת when it comes.

phrases.english: But Hillel the Elder
had a different trait
that all his actions were for the sake of Heaven
as it says: 'Blessed is ה׳ day by day'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הִלֵּל הַזָּקֵן מִדָּה אַחֶרֶת הָיְתָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts הלל's approach with שמאי's approach from step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל trusted ה׳ daily rather than setting aside food for שבת all week

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the two approaches
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא states the same split in general terms: בית שמאי prepare for שבת from Sunday, and בית הלל say 'ברוך ה׳ יום יום'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. בית שמאי say: from the first day of the week, prepare for your שבת. בית הלל say: 'Blessed is ה׳ day by day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that supports what was just said about שמאי and הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6 and 7 described what the two individual teachers did. This ברייתא shows that their schools, בית שמאי and בית הלל, held these same two approaches. So it is a general view of each school, not just a personal habit.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא also teaches this (supporting source)
from the first day of your week, prepare for your שבת

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי prepare for שבת all week long. בית הלל trust ה׳ to provide day by day.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a baraita
Beit Shammai say:
From the first day of your week, prepare for your Shabbat
And Beit Hillel say:
'Blessed is ה׳ day by day'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports steps 6 and 7 with a parallel ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: The contrast between שמאי's and הלל's approaches to preparing for שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting בית שמאי and בית הלל

steps.title: A giver does not need to tell the receiver about a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches that someone giving a gift does not need to inform the receiver. His proof is משה, whose face shone without his knowing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: someone who gives a gift to his friend does not need to tell him. As it says: 'And משה did not know that the skin of his face was shining.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new statement. It connects to the earlier topic through the theme of honoring שבת, which comes up in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ gave משה a gift, a shining face, and did not tell him about it. From this, רבי חמא learns that a giver is not required to announce his gift.

keyTerms.meaning: the skin of his face shone

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
One who gives a gift to his friend
does not need to inform him
as it says: 'And Moshe did not know
that the skin of his face was shining'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about gifts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A giver need not inform the receiver of a gift

steps.title: Challenge: the gift of שבת had to be announced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: ה׳ told משה to go and inform ישראל about the gift of שבת. From this, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל learns that one who gives bread to a child must tell the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: the פסוק says 'to know that I am ה׳ who makes you holy.' ה׳ said to משה: 'משה, I have a good gift in My treasure house, and its name is שבת. I want to give it to ישראל. Go and tell them.' From here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: one who gives bread to a child must tell his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי חמא's rule with a source that says the opposite: a giver does need to inform.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חמא said a giver does not have to tell the receiver. Here, ה׳ made a point of announcing the gift of שבת. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל even turns this into a practical rule: tell the child's mother about the bread you gave him. So the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from a tannaitic source)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'To know that I am ה׳ who sanctifies you'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe:

phrases.aramaic: מֹשֶׁה! מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי בְּבֵית גְּנָזַי
phrases.english: Moshe! I have a good gift in My treasure house
and its name is Shabbat
and I wish to give it to Israel
Go and inform them

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: From here Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
One who gives bread to a child
must inform his mother

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חמא's rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חמא's rule that a giver need not inform
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ה׳ announced the gift of שבת, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires telling the mother, so a giver must inform

steps.title: Answer: gifts that will be noticed vs. gifts that won't
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction. A gift that will become known anyway needs no announcement. A gift that will not become known must be announced.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is a gift that will be revealed on its own. That case is a gift that will not be revealed on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the two sources into two different kinds of gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's shining face would obviously be noticed, since people would see it and tell him. So there was no need to tell him. Bread given to a child might never come to the mother's attention, so the giver must tell her.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is about a gift that is likely to be revealed
that is about a gift that is not likely to be revealed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by type of gift)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources contradict each other about whether to inform
steps.terutzMaskana: No need to inform about a gift that will be revealed anyway; you must inform about a hidden one

steps.title: But שבת is also an obvious gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: שבת is also a gift that would become known, so why did ה׳ need to announce it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But שבת is also a gift that will be revealed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the new distinction, an obvious gift needs no announcement. ישראל would certainly learn about שבת, since they would be commanded to keep it. So why did ה׳ tell משה to announce it?

phrases.english: Shabbat too is a gift that is likely to be revealed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between revealed and unrevealed gifts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבת would obviously be known, yet it was announced

steps.title: The reward of שבת is hidden
steps.stepSummary: שבת itself would become known, but its reward would not. That is why ה׳ had it announced.
steps.simpleTranslation: The giving of its reward is not something that will be revealed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge, and the distinction from step 11 stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The existence of שבת is obvious, but the great reward for keeping it is hidden. Because that part of the gift would not be revealed on its own, ה׳ told משה to announce it.
steps.whatToRemember: No need to announce a gift that will be noticed anyway. You must announce a hidden gift. שבת was announced because its reward is hidden.

phrases.english: Its reward is not likely to be revealed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining which part of the gift is hidden
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת is an obvious gift, so it should not have needed an announcement
steps.terutzMaskana: The reward of שבת is hidden, so it needed to be announced

steps.title: How exactly do you let the mother know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the rule of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, that one who gives bread to a child must inform the mother. It then asks how this is done in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: From here רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said, 'One who gives bread to a child must let his mother know.' What does he do to the child to let her know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line quoted earlier (Step 10) so it can ask a practical question about it. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, this rule was only used as proof that a hidden gift must be announced. Now the גמרא asks a practical question. A small child cannot be relied on to report the gift, so how does the giver actually get the message to the mother?

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said' – a formula that re-quotes an earlier statement in order to discuss it further
To inform, to let someone know

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא is deliberately re-quoting the rule from Step 10 to ask how it works in real life.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר, מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: The Master said: From here Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
phrases.notes: 'From here' = from the verse telling משה to inform ישראל about שבת.

phrases.english: One who gives bread to a child
must inform his mother.
phrases.notes: So the mother knows who loves her child, and the giver earns her goodwill.

phrases.english: What does he do to him?
phrases.notes: In other words, how does he make sure the mother finds out?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the rule quoted in Step 10 to clarify how it is carried out in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical method by which the giver informs the child's mother.

steps.title: Put oil and eye-paint on the child
steps.stepSummary: The giver rubs oil on the child and paints his eyes with כחול (eye-paint). The mother will notice and ask, and the child will tell her who did it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He rubs oil on him and fills his eyes with eye-paint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the giver leaves a visible sign on the child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil and eye-paint are clues the mother cannot miss. When she asks the child who did this, he will say who it was, and she will learn that this person was also kind to him with bread. The sign turns a hidden gift into a known one.

keyTerms.meaning: Eye-paint (כחול, a dark cosmetic for the eyes)

phrases.english: He rubs oil on him
and fills [his eyes] with eye-paint.
phrases.notes: The mother will notice and ask the child about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the practical question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leave a visible sign on the child (oil and eye-paint) so the mother asks and finds out.

steps.title: What about today, when people fear witchcraft?
steps.stepSummary: Nowadays people worry about כשפים (witchcraft), so a stranger painting a child's eyes would look suspicious. What should one do instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: And nowadays, when we are concerned about witchcraft, what should he do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question: the old method may not work today. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a stranger puts things on a child's eyes, a worried mother may suspect sorcery instead of feeling grateful. So the method from Step 15 could backfire, and the גמרא looks for a safer sign.

phrases.english: And nowadays, when we are concerned about witchcraft, what [should he do]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a practical problem with the method given in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A method of informing the mother that will not raise fears of witchcraft.

steps.title: רב פפא: Smear on some of the same food
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says to rub a little of the food itself (whatever was on the bread) onto the child. The mother will see it and realize someone gave him food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: He rubs on him some of that same type of food.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a safe sign that still lets the mother know about the gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food on a child's face looks like an ordinary snack, not sorcery. It still tells the mother that someone fed her child, so the purpose of informing her is kept without the danger.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the updated practical method

steps.whatToRemember: A gift that will not be noticed should be made known. For a child, leave a harmless sign, like a bit of the food itself, so the mother finds out.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
He rubs on him some of that same type [of food].
phrases.notes: For example, a bit of the butter or spread from the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שָׁיֵיף לֵיהּ מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16 and closes the practical discussion of informing the mother.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Smear a bit of the food itself on the child. It is a harmless, recognizable sign.

steps.title: All מצוות were given publicly, except שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, teaches that every מצוה was given to ישראל in public, except שבת, which was given in private. The source is the פסוק 'Between Me and בני ישראל it is a sign forever.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: All the מצוות that הקדוש ברוך הוא gave to ישראל, He gave them in public, except שבת, which He gave them in private. As it says: 'Between Me and בני ישראל it is a sign forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about the gift of שבת: it was given privately, as a personal sign between ה׳ and ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'between Me and בני ישראל' show that שבת is like a private sign between two close parties. This also helps explain the earlier steps. Because שבת was given privately, ה׳ had to tell משה to inform ישראל about it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the coming question. If שבת was 'secret' to ישראל, what responsibility do the nations have regarding it?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִצְוֹת שֶׁנָּתַן לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: All the מצוות that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave to Israel —
He gave them in public,
except for Shabbat, which He gave them in private,
as it is stated: "Between Me and the children of Israel
it is a sign forever."
phrases.notes: שמות לא:יז. 'Between Me and them' implies something private.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching about the gift of שבת, connected to the theme of hidden gifts and announcing them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All מצוות were given publicly, except שבת, which was given privately, as derived from 'בֵּינִי וּבֵין בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל'.

steps.title: If שבת was secret, why are the nations held responsible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if שבת was given in private, the nations should not be punished in connection with it, because you cannot hold someone responsible for something hidden from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the nations should not be punished regarding it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן יוחי's teaching. Calling שבת 'private' seems to clash with the nations having any responsibility about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is simple: being responsible requires knowing. If שבת was completely hidden, the nations could not be punished in connection with it. Yet we assume they can be. (רש״י connects this to the rule that a גוי who keeps שבת is liable. Sefaria explains it as punishment for refusing to accept it. Either way, the point is that secrecy should remove responsibility.)

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, לָא לִעַנְשׁוּ גּוֹיִם עֲלַהּ?
phrases.english: If so, the nations should not be punished regarding it!
phrases.notes: 'It' refers to שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לָא לִעַנְשׁוּ גּוֹיִם עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of Step 18 that שבת was given privately.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that שבת was given בצנעא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hidden information cannot create responsibility. If שבת was private, the nations should have no liability regarding it.

steps.title: שבת was made known, but not its reward
steps.stepSummary: The nations were told about שבת itself. Only the reward for keeping it was kept private.
steps.simpleTranslation: שבת itself, He did inform them about. The reward for it, He did not inform them about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'private' part was only the reward, not שבת itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows what 'בצנעא' means. The existence of שבת was public enough to create responsibility, but the reward was the secret. This matches Step 13, where the reward of שבת was also the part that needed special announcing.

phrases.english: Shabbat — He did inform them [about it],
its reward — He did not inform them.
phrases.notes: Only the reward was the 'private' part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of 'בצנעא' to the reward only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת itself was hidden, so the nations could not be responsible.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת was made known. Only its reward was hidden, so responsibility remains.

steps.title: Another answer: only the נשמה יתירה was kept secret
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even the reward was made known. What stayed private was the נשמה יתירה, the extra soul given on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: its reward was also made known to them, but the extra soul, He did not inform them about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to answer the question. It moves the 'secret' part of שבת to a different detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, both שבת and its reward were public. The private gift is the נשמה יתירה. That is the inner gift ה׳ shares only with ישראל, which fits the idea of a 'sign between Me and בני ישראל'.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say – introduces an alternative answer

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
its reward He also informed them about,
the additional soul — He did not inform them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: מַתַּן שְׂכָרָהּ נָמֵי אוֹדְעִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, alternative answer to the קשיא of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative identification of the hidden element
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reward was the hidden part (first answer).
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the reward was public. The hidden gift is the נשמה יתירה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: The extra soul comes on ערב שבת and leaves after שבת
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that ה׳ gives a person an extra soul on ערב שבת and takes it back at מוצאי שבת. He learns this from 'שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַשׁ', read as 'once שבת ends, woe, the soul is lost.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: הקדוש ברוך הוא gives a person an extra soul on ערב שבת, and at מוצאי שבת it is taken from him. As it says, 'He rested and was refreshed (וַיִּנָּפַשׁ)': once he has rested, woe (וַי), the soul (נֶפֶשׁ) is lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that the נשמה יתירה, mentioned in the second answer, is real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads the word וַיִּנָּפַשׁ as two words: 'וַי' (woe) + 'נֶפֶשׁ' (soul). When שבת is over, we lose the extra soul, and that is the 'woe'. This shows the נשמה יתירה is an actual gift ה׳ gives on שבת, the one the second answer says stayed private.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, the אמורא who teaches about the extra soul
'And was refreshed', expounded as וַי + נֶפֶשׁ (woe, the soul)

steps.whatToRemember: שבת is a gift between ה׳ and ישראל. Its private, inner part is the נשמה יתירה, an extra soul that comes on ערב שבת and leaves at מוצאי שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: The דרשה is a wordplay. וַיִּנָּפַשׁ is read as 'וַי אָבְדָה נֶפֶשׁ' (woe, the soul is lost). It is not the plain meaning 'was refreshed'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the classic source for the נשמה יתירה. It is also why בשמים are smelled at הבדלה, to comfort us for the loss of the extra soul.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: נְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה נוֹתֵן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: An additional soul the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives
in a person on Shabbat eve,
and at the conclusion of Shabbat it is taken from him,
as it is stated: "He rested and was refreshed,"
phrases.notes: שמות לא:יז, the same פסוק as the 'sign' in Step 18.

phrases.english: once he has rested [and שבת is over],
woe, the soul is lost.
phrases.notes: וַיִּנָּפַשׁ is read as וַי + נֶפֶשׁ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second answer (Step 21) by establishing that the נשמה יתירה exists.
steps.raayaObject: The existence of the נשמה יתירה, the hidden gift of שבת mentioned in Step 21.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's דרשה on 'שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַשׁ' (שמות לא:יז).

steps.title: אביי: only a cooked dish works, not bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about preparing a תבשיל on ערב יום טוב. אביי says this only works with a cooked dish, not with bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a person makes a cooked dish on ערב יום טוב. אביי said: they only taught this about a cooked dish, but bread does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: After the side discussion about שבת, the גמרא returns to the משנה about עירובי תבשילין. אביי teaches a limit: the food set aside must be a תבשיל, not bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word תבשיל, a cooked dish. אביי reads this word precisely: bread alone is not good enough for the עירוב. This sets up the next question, which asks what is wrong with bread.

keyTerms.meaning: food set aside on ערב יום טוב so that one may cook on יום טוב for שבת
they only taught this about…, a formula that limits a rule

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשֶׂה אָדָם תַּבְשִׁיל מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: A person makes a cooked dish from the eve of the Festival.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They taught this only about a cooked dish,
but bread, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא תַּבְשִׁיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the aggadic discussion of שבת to the משנה's halacha of עירובי תבשילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירובי תבשילין must be a cooked dish; bread alone is not valid.

steps.title: Why does bread not work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes bread different.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about bread, that it does not work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's rule. This line sets up the attempts to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread is real, important food, so it is not obvious why it should fail. The גמרא wants to know exactly which quality bread is missing.

phrases.english: What is different about bread, that it does not work?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind אביי's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason bread is excluded from עירובי תבשילין.

steps.title: First suggestion: the עירוב must be a side dish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the עירוב must be something eaten with bread, and bread is not eaten with bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you say that we need something that goes along with bread, and bread does not go along with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason: the עירוב must be a side dish that you eat together with bread. This is only a suggestion, and the גמרא is about to test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a תבשיל is the kind of food that accompanies bread at a meal. Bread cannot accompany itself, so it fails. The word אילימא signals that this suggestion will probably be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: if you will say, introducing a suggestion that is about to be challenged
a side dish eaten together with bread

phrases.english: If you say we require something that accompanies bread,
and bread does not accompany bread,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a tentative answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tentative: the עירוב must be a side dish (מלפת), and bread is not.

steps.title: But porridge is not a side dish either, and it works
steps.stepSummary: Porridge is also not a side dish, as רבי זירא shows. Yet רב נחומי בר זכריה quotes אביי that one may make an עירוב with porridge.
steps.simpleTranslation: But porridge is also not a side dish, as רבי זירא said: those foolish Babylonians eat bread with bread. And רב נחומי בר זכריה said in the name of אביי: one may make an עירוב with porridge!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the side-dish suggestion. Porridge is not a side dish, yet אביי himself allows it as an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Porridge is made from grain, so eating it with bread is like eating bread with bread, as רבי זירא mocked. If the rule were 'it must be a side dish,' porridge should fail. Since אביי allows porridge, side-dish cannot be his reason.

phrases.english: But porridge also does not accompany bread,
as Rabbi Zeira said:
These foolish Babylonians
who eat bread with bread.
phrases.notes: They eat bread with porridge, which is also a grain food.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: And Rav Nechumi bar Zekharya said in the name of Abaye:
One may make an eiruv with porridge!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the side-dish suggestion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the עירוב must be a מלפת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Porridge is not a מלפת, as רבי זירא shows, yet אביי allows it. So מלפת cannot be the requirement.

steps.title: Real reason: the עירוב must be something unusual
steps.stepSummary: The עירוב must be something not eaten routinely. Bread is routine; porridge is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we need something that is not common. Bread is common, and porridge is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the side-dish idea and gives a new reason. The עירוב must be a food that is not routine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you set aside ordinary bread, no one can tell it was put aside for an עירוב. An unusual food like porridge stands out, so it is clear it was set aside on purpose. This fits אביי's ruling that porridge works.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, introducing a new answer after the first one failed

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: bread fails because it is too ordinary (שכיח). Porridge works because it is unusual.

phrases.english: Rather: we require something that is not common,
and bread is common,
and porridge is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion with a new reason that fits the porridge ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עירוב must be a side dish.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עירוב must be something not routine, so it is clearly set aside.

steps.title: Second version: אביי's same rule restated
steps.stepSummary: Another version reports the same statement of אביי, but with a different discussion after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: אביי said, they only taught this about a cooked dish, but bread does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second version of the whole discussion. אביי's rule is the same; what follows will be different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself does not change. The two versions disagree about the reason and about how רב נחומי quoted אביי on porridge. This line sets up the second line of reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: some say, introducing a different version of the discussion

phrases.english: Some say,
Abaye said:
They taught this only about a cooked dish,
but bread, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts an alternate version of the discussion from step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same ruling: bread alone is not valid for עירובי תבשילין.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks why bread is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: In this version, the גמרא again asks for אביי's reason. This sets up the attempts that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question as step 24, but here the answers will be tested in the opposite order.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the restated rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason bread is excluded, according to the second version.

steps.title: Suggestion: the עירוב must be unusual
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason is that the עירוב must be something not routine, and bread is routine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you say that we need something that is not common, and bread is common.
steps.whatsHappening: This version first tries the reason that was accepted in version 1. Here it is only a suggestion, about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In version 1 this was the final answer. In version 2, the same idea is tested first and will be knocked down.

phrases.english: If you say that we require something that is not common,
and bread is common,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a tentative answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Tentative: the עירוב must be something not routine.

steps.title: But porridge is unusual, and it does not work
steps.stepSummary: Porridge is not routine, yet in this version רב נחומי quotes אביי that one may NOT make an עירוב with porridge.
steps.simpleTranslation: But porridge is not common, and רב נחומי בר זכריה said in the name of אביי: one may not make an עירוב with porridge!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'unusual' reason. Porridge is unusual, yet according to this version אביי does not allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being unusual were the rule, porridge should work. Since אביי forbids it here, being unusual cannot be his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: one may not make an עירוב

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions quote רב נחומי בר זכריה in opposite ways. In version 1 he says מערבין, one may use porridge. In version 2 he says אין מערבין, one may not. This difference is the entire reason the two versions reach different explanations.

phrases.english: But porridge is not common,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: and Rav Nechumi bar Zekharya said in the name of Abaye:
One may not make an eiruv with porridge!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'unusual' suggestion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the עירוב must be לא שכיח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Porridge is unusual, yet אביי forbids it in this version, so being unusual is not the requirement.

steps.title: Real reason: the עירוב must be a side dish
steps.stepSummary: The עירוב must be a side dish. Neither bread nor porridge is a side dish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we need something that goes along with bread. Bread does not go along with bread, and porridge also does not go along with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the side-dish reason as the answer in this version. It explains why both bread and porridge fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason fits the version-2 quote that porridge is not allowed. Porridge, being grain, is like bread, so it is no side dish.

phrases.english: Rather: we require something that accompanies bread,
and bread does not accompany bread,
and porridge also does not accompany bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason with the side-dish reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עירוב must be something unusual.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עירוב must be a מלפת; bread and porridge both fail.

steps.title: Proof that porridge is like bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא's remark shows that eating porridge with bread counts as eating bread with bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי זירא said: those foolish Babylonians eat bread with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי זירא's remark to prove that porridge is not a side dish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא calls the Babylonians foolish for eating bread with porridge, which he calls 'bread with bread.' So porridge has the status of bread, not of a side dish.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: Version 2: bread fails because it is not a side dish (מלפת). Porridge also fails, because it is like bread.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Zeira said:
These foolish Babylonians
who eat bread with bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: הָנֵי בַּבְלָאֵי טַפְשָׁאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim that porridge is not a side dish.
steps.raayaObject: That דייסא is not a מלפת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא's remark about the Babylonians eating bread with bread.

steps.title: Leftover lentils at the bottom of a pot work
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that leftover lentils at the bottom of a pot can be the עירוב, as long as there is a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: lentils at the bottom of a pot, one may rely on them for עירובי תבשילין. This applies only if there is a כזית of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new teaching. Even leftover lentils that happen to be in a pot can serve as the עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food does not have to be cooked especially for the עירוב. Leftovers count as a תבשיל, but there must be at least a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: an olive's volume, a minimum amount

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya taught:
Lentils that are at the bottom of a pot,
one may rely on them for the joining of cooked foods.
And this applies only if they contain an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: עֲדָשִׁים שֶׁבְּשׁוּלֵי קְדֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: what minimal or leftover foods count as a תבשיל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover lentils at the bottom of a pot may be used for עירובי תבשילין if there is a כזית.

steps.title: Fat scraped off a knife works too
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה teaches that fat scraped off a knife can be the עירוב, as long as there is a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה said: fat that is on a knife, one scrapes it off and relies on it for עירובי תבשילין. This applies only if there is a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: A similar teaching: even fat stuck to a knife can serve as the עירוב if you scrape it off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the lentils, this is an unplanned leftover, and it still counts as cooked food. The same minimum of a כזית applies.
steps.whatToRemember: Even small leftovers, like lentils in a pot or fat on a knife, can be an עירובי תבשילין, as long as there is a כזית.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda said:
Fat that is on a knife,
one scrapes it off and relies on it
for the joining of cooked foods.
And this applies only if there is an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה: שַׁמְנוּנִית שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הַסַּכִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case to רבי חייא's lentils.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fat scraped from a knife may be used for עירובי תבשילין if there is a כזית.

steps.title: Small salted fish are not considered food cooked by a gentile
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי quotes רב: small salted fish do not fall under the prohibition of בישולי גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רב: small salted fish do not have any problem of food cooked by a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching. Small salted fish that a גוי cooked are not forbidden as בישולי גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The salting already makes these small fish edible. A גוי cooking them does not turn them into food, because they were already food. The prohibition of בישולי גוים applies when a גוי's cooking is what makes the food fit to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Food cooked by a non-Jew, which the Rabbis forbade
There is no problem of (this prohibition)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רב יוסף's next point, which applies this rule to עירוב תבשילין.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rav said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line, merged into this statement.

phrases.english: Small salted fish
phrases.notes: These are already edible because of the salting.

phrases.english: do not have the problem of food cooked by gentiles.
phrases.notes: Even if a גוי cooked them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the foods that can serve as the עירוב (steps 34-35), the גמרא brings a new ruling about fish cooked by a גוי. רב יוסף will connect it to עירוב תבשילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Small salted fish cooked by a גוי are not forbidden as בישולי גוים, because they were already edible.

steps.title: Roasted salted fish work for עירובי תבשילין, but fish fried in batter are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף: if a גוי roasted the small salted fish, a Jew may use them for עירוב תבשילין. If the גוי made them into כסא דהרסנא, they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: even if a גוי roasted them, a Jew may rely on them for עירוב תבשילין. But if the גוי made them into a dish of fish fried in oil and flour, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף builds on רב's rule and gives two cases. Roasted fish are still allowed and can even be used for עירוב תבשילין. Fish fried in a batter of oil and flour are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simple roasting does not change the status of fish that were already edible, so they are not בישולי גוים and can serve as the cooked dish for the עירוב. Frying them with oil and flour creates a new, important dish. Here the גוי's cooking really made the food, so it falls under בישולי גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: One may rely on them (use them)
The cooked dish set aside before יום טוב so one may cook on יום טוב for שבת
A dish of small fish fried in oil and flour

steps.confusionAlert: The same fish get different rulings because of what the גוי did to them. Plain roasting changes nothing important, so they stay permitted. Frying them in a batter of oil and flour makes them a new, special dish, so they become forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
And even if a gentile roasted them,
one may rely on them for the joining of cooked foods.
phrases.notes: They are not בישולי גוים, so they count as a usable cooked dish.

phrases.english: But if a gentile made them
phrases.notes: This contrasts with the roasting case.

phrases.english: into fish fried with oil and flour, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This is a new, important dish, so it is בישולי גוים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: וְאִם צְלָאָן גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This applies רב's rule from step 36 to עירוב תבשילין and limits it with the case of כסא דהרסנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roasted small salted fish may be used for עירוב תבשילין. Fish made by a גוי into כסא דהרסנא are forbidden as בישולי גוים.

steps.title: The גמרא objects that the ruling is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: once רב said these fish are not בישולי גוים, it is obvious that roasted ones may be used for עירובי תבשילין. So why did רב יוסף need to teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that רב יוסף's ruling, that roasted salted fish may be relied on for עירובי תבשילין, is too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב already said these fish are not בישולי גוים, and roasting makes them a cooked food. So it seems plain that they can serve as the עירוב. The גמרא assumes every teaching must add something new, so it asks what this one adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (the teaching seems unnecessary)

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: This challenges the need to teach the ruling at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks the need for רב יוסף's ruling in step 37 that roasted fish may be used for עירובי תבשילין.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that roasted salted fish may be relied on for עירובי תבשילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since רב ruled these fish are not בישולי גוים, it follows automatically that a roasted one is a valid cooked dish for the עירוב, so stating it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The גמרא begins explaining why the ruling was needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its answer with 'מהו דתימא', meaning 'you might have thought'. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא begins its answer by presenting a mistaken thought someone could have had, and that thought continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מהו דתימא' introduces a reasonable but wrong assumption. The teaching was needed to rule it out. Wait for the next lines to see what that assumption is.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption the teaching comes to reject)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer is not finished here. It continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Lest you say that:
phrases.notes: Opens the answer; it continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins the answer to the 'פשיטא' challenge in step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: הוה אמינא setup (shows the teaching is needed to reject a plausible mistake)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Not yet stated; it continues on the next amud.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated; it continues on the next amud.
